transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lina Morales (Redwood AE), Jasper Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood CSM), Ethan Park (Argosy VP Eng), Simone Alvarez (Argosy SRE Lead), Priya Nair (Argosy Security)

Summary:
- Postmortem follow-up for Incident #4522 (partial outage of inference tier affecting patient-facing triage feature). Discussed root cause, mitigations in prod, reliability improvements and next steps.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and root cause hypothesis (KV cache eviction + autoscaler race)
- Short-term mitigations (config rollbacks, dedicated pool burst)
- Medium/long-term reliability items (runbooks, canary policies, fallback model variants, better metrics)
- Compliance/artifacts requested

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina M: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the follow-up to incident four five two two, quick recap then go into root cause and next steps, jasper do you want to start with the timeline?
[00:18] Jasper K: yeah, quick timeline. at 02:12 UTC we saw p50 latencies jump, by 02:17 p95 spiked and then at 02:20 we started dropping requests. It correlated with a spike in concurrent sessions hitting the triage route. There was also a burst of cache misses on the KV cache, which led to more GPU warmups and then the autoscaler thrash.
[00:39] Simone A: just to interrupt, we saw the same thing in our dashboards, the health checks were flapping and some pods recreated, looked like the K V cash was being evicted, might be a memory OOM on the smaller pods.
[00:52] Jasper K: yes, memory pressure on the worker class caused eviction. the eviction exposed a race in how the autoscaler decides to spin up dedicated workers vs reusing warm pools. Essentially we had two factors: burst of requests + prefix caching cold start.
[01:10] Ethan P: can you clarify "prefix caching cold start"? that's internal wording, i think.
[01:16] Jasper K: right sorry, prefix/KV cache is where we keep recurrent tokens and K V entries. when those are evicted the runtime has to recompute KV state which costs tokens and gpu time, warming the KV is expensive. that combined with autoscale thresholds let queue grow and some requests time out.
[01:35] Priya N: from security/compliance angle we need timestamps and the list of logs we can get, SOC two artifacts, and KMS access patterns around the keys used at the time. we also need confirmation whether any PHI was written to logs.
[01:50] Maya S: we've started the ingress of those logs to the secure bucket and flagged sensitive fields. we'll coordinate with you on access.
[02:02] Lina M: quick question for argosy on business impact - ethan?
[02:06] Ethan P: we saw ~18 minutes of degraded service for triage. about 1200 triage requests impacted, estimated revenue/clinical impact priority is medium-high; we had to fall back to manual triage for some clinics.
[02:20] Jasper K: right, so cause summary: KV eviction + memory pressure on smaller worker shape + autoscaler policy that reacts too slowly + model warmup cost. recommended short-term: pin the triage route to a dedicated pool during peak hours, increase worker memory threshold, and tweak autoscale sensitivity.
[02:38] Simone A: we applied a config change at 03:05 to increase memory reservation and forced a scale-up to remove the pressure, that stabilized the fleet. there was also a canary rollback applied at 03:22 where we flipped back an inference runtime change.
[02:54] Lina M: good, what about the fallback model? we heard some requests were routed to a smaller quantized model which degraded quality, is that accurate?
[03:03] Jasper K: yes some traffic hit the q4-lite variant when the primary pool exhausted capacity; that reduced quality. as part of mitigation we added a routing rule to prefer returning an error or queued response rather than swapping to that variant for triage until we validate output.
[03:22] Ethan P: we prefer degradation over wrong triage outputs.
[03:25] Priya N: on compliance, are the logs scrubbed for PHI?
[03:29] Maya S: yes logs in the shared bucket are redacted, raw traces remain in customer-owned S3 we can whitelist access. we'll send process docs.
[03:40] Simone A: can i ask a technical question: the autoscaler threshold - is that per-customer or a global setting on the cluster?
[03:46] Jasper K: currently it's per-nodepool but same policy template for all customers; we can push per-customer overrides, in fact we recommended a per-customer aggressive policy for Argosy to avoid this kind of thrash.
[03:59] Lina M: what about monitoring/alerts, we want earlier detection. right now our alerting triggered when 4xx/5xx rose; can we alert on eviction or queue growth?
[04:08] Jasper K: yes we can add probes for kv-miss-rate and GPU-util tail percentiles; set a moderate alert before downstream 5xx spike. we'll add a dashboard panel and an alert rule.
[04:20] Ethan P: timeline wise, how quickly can we get a short-term dedicated pool? cost-wise we'd take a burst for the month if needed.
[04:27] Lina M: (AE) we can provision dedicated burst capacity; i'll share pricing. short-term we can enable a reserved pool for triage route for evenings and mornings.
[04:36] Maya S: we'll propose two options: short-term dedicated burst (1-2 weeks) and mid-term dedicated reserved (monthly) depending on traffic pattern.
[04:44] Priya N: also, need audit logs and proof of patching for the runtime. do you rotate keys through KMS/HSM? any change during the incident window?
[04:53] Jasper K: no key rotation occurred at the time; KMS usage logs show no unusual activity. we will extract KMS access logs and provide them.
[05:02] Simone A: for the longer-term action: we need playbooks and canary policies. i'd like an automated rollback window and a synthetic canary traffic generator to verify model quality before broad rollout.
[05:15] Jasper K: agreed. our proposed reliability improvements: 1) per-route dedicated pools for critical endpoints, 2) prefix/KV caching improvements with persistent cache reservations, 3) improved autoscaler with hysteresis, 4) better fallbacks (return queue/error vs degrade model), 5) runbook + synthetic canaries and periodic chaos testing.
[05:34] Ethan P: can you quantify cost delta for dedicated pool?
[05:37] Lina M: we'll send a delta estimate; jasper will run benchmarks with your traffic profile to estimate tokens and GPU hours.
[05:43] Jasper K: i'll run a benchmark against a small dedicated pool (g4x-equivalent) and a burst pool and share results by end of week.
[05:51] Simone A: also curious about VPC/private deployment options; is the private product able to run on premise for full isolation? we have regulatory customers.
[05:59] Lina M: yes Redwood Private supports VPC + on-prem packaging, but that's a bigger lift. we can discuss timeline if that's a direction. note: moving to Private also changes observability and might need on-prem sizing.
[06:14] Priya N: for SOC2 and ISO artifacts, who should i reach out to?
[06:18] Maya S: send requests to csm-security@redwood.ai and i'll own delivery, plus we'll open a sharing link for the audit folder.
[06:27] Ethan P: ok next steps summary?
[06:30] Lina M: jasper share logs/metrics and benchmark, maya schedule runbook review, i send pricing for dedicated burst, priya confirm compliance asks; all targeted within this week unless noted.
[06:42] Jasper K: quick technical note: there's a known issue in the autoscaler where scale-in happens too fast when ephemeral memory spikes occur; we will add a 60s hysteresis by default and allow per-customer override.
[06:55] Simone A: that sounds good. one more ask: can we get p99 traces for the model entrypoint only and a sample of the dropped requests?
[07:02] Jasper K: yes we'll provide p99 traces and samples, redacted for PHI.
[07:09] Ethan P: any risk that fixing autoscaler could raise cost materially?
[07:13] Jasper K: there is some cost, but we can tune to balance cost vs reliability; also Optimize recommendations can reduce overall token spend by better batching and cache suggestions.
[07:24] Lina M: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a written postmortem doc and action item tracker.

Recap & explicit next steps (spoken):
- Jasper: collect host-level GPU metrics, KV miss traces, p99/p95 traces, and run benchmark with Argosy triage workload (due 2026-12-08).
- Maya: schedule runbook + on-call playbook review with Simone and team (due 2026-12-13).
- Lina: share pricing for dedicated burst and short-term contract options (due 2026-12-07).
- Priya/Ethan: confirm impacted endpoints and business impact numbers and compliance artifact requests (due 2026-12-09).

Action items (in transcript):
[07:50] Jasper K: action - i'll upload logs to the secure share and message PRiya and Maya when ready.
[08:02] Maya S: i'll take the runbook scheduling and invite argosy SREs.
[08:15] Lina M: i'll get pricing over; expect email tomorrow.

Links & shared artifacts mentioned:
- Incident timeline doc (internal link) - will be shared via secure share
- Benchmark worksheet (sheet) - Redwood to populate with results

End of call at ~15:55 UTC.
